'''Carol Saunders Wood''' (born February 9, 1945)<ref name="ams">[https://www.ams.org/notices/200608/bios06.pdf Candidate biography], Trustee election, [[American Mathematical Society]], ''Notices of the AMS'' 53 (8): 930, September 2006.</ref> is a retired American mathematician, the [[Edward Burr Van Vleck]] Professor of Mathematics, ''Emerita'', at [[Wesleyan University]].<ref>[http://www.wesleyan.edu/mathcs/whoswho/index.html Mathematics and Computer Science faculty listing], Wesleyan, retrieved January 2, 2015.</ref> Her research concerns [[mathematical logic]] and [[model theory|model-theoretic]] [[abstract algebra|algebra]],<ref name="cv">[http://cwood.web.wesleyan.edu/cv.htm Curriculum vitae], retrieved January 2, 2015.</ref> and in particular the theory of [[differentially closed field]]s.<ref>{{citation|title=A Guide to Classical and Modern Model Theory|volume=19|series=Trends in Logic|first1=Annalisa|last1=Marcja| first2=Carlo |last2=Toffalori |publisher=Springer |year=2003 |isbn=9781402013317|page=115|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=H0YYhu3DHh0C&pg=PA115}}.</ref>

Wood graduated in 1966 from [[Randolph College|Randolph-Macon Woman's College]], a small [[United Methodist Church|United Methodist]] college in [[Lynchburg, Virginia]].<ref name="cv"/> She earned her doctorate in 1971 from [[Yale University]] with a dissertation on [[Forcing (mathematics)|forcing]] supervised by [[Abraham Robinson]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|name=Carol Saunders Wood|id=38885}}</ref> At Wesleyan, she served three times as department chair.<ref name="ams"/> She was an [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Council member at large from 1987 to 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> She was president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from 1991 to 1993,<ref name="cv"/> and served on the board of trustees of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 2002 to 2007.<ref name="ams"/> She has served on the AMS Committee on Women in Mathematics since it was formed in 2012 and was chair from 2012 to 2015.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/cowim-past.html Committee on Women in Mathematics (CoWIM) Past Members], retrieved March 22, 2020</ref> She supervised 4 doctoral students at Wesleyan.<ref name="mg"/>

Wood was the 1998 commencement speaker for mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>[https://math.berkeley.edu/about/events/commencement/speakers-past Commencement Speakers Past], Berkeley mathematics, retrieved January 2, 2015.</ref> In 2012, she became one of the inaugural fellows of the American Mathematical Society.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved January 2, 2015.</ref> In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|website=awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=9 January 2021}}</ref>
